domain_characteristics.detection_complexity: high - attacks use sophisticated HTML obfuscation, mimic legitimate sites, and employ social engineering

common_indicators: presence of hidden or obfuscated JavaScript for geolocation or browser manipulation
login forms with suspicious or non-standard action URLs (e.g., 'free.php', 'media', 'process.php')
URLs with domain names unrelated to the claimed brand or with suspicious subdomains
usage of embedded tracking or pixel images with hidden 1x1 size
mismatch between page content and URL domain (e.g., 'Telekom Login' content on 'communityhomecare.org')
attack_signatures: phishing pages mimicking legitimate login portals with fake credential forms posting to non-official endpoints
JavaScript code that intercepts or fakes browser geolocation APIs to evade detection or fingerprinting
Use of hidden input fields and anti-automation techniques in login forms
Embedding of external stylesheets and scripts from legitimate domains to appear authentic
Use of social engineering text and brand names (e.g., 'Telekom Login', 'Instagram', 'Telegram Web') with mismatched URLs
technical_markers: form action URLs containing uncommon or suspicious filenames (e.g., 'free.php', 'process.php')
presence of multiple hidden 1x1 pixel images for tracking or data exfiltration
JavaScript functions overriding native browser APIs (e.g., navigator.geolocation)
URLs with excessive subdomain levels or unusual TLDs (e.g., 'instagram-verification-com-0fb9d4d5c638e553c69258afdd617c17.netlify.app')
HTML title and meta description mismatches with actual domain
attack_vectors: web-based phishing via fake login pages
social engineering through deceptive UI and content
credential harvesting via form submission to attacker-controlled endpoints
malicious redirects and tracking via embedded scripts and images
exploit_techniques: API hooking and overriding (e.g., geolocation API) to evade detection
Use of hidden form fields and obfuscated JavaScript to bypass automated analysis
Domain impersonation and URL obfuscation to mimic legitimate services
Embedding legitimate external resources to increase trust
Use of pixel tracking for user monitoring

typical_behaviors: HTML pages with consistent domain and content branding
Login forms with standard action URLs pointing to official domains
Use of standard meta tags and consistent language and charset declarations
Presence of legitimate external scripts and stylesheets from trusted domains
No hidden or obfuscated JavaScript overriding browser APIs
baseline_metrics: form action URLs matching domain or subdomain of the site
absence of hidden 1x1 pixel images used for tracking
consistent use of HTTPS and valid certificates
URL structure with expected domain names and no excessive subdomains
HTML content size and structure consistent with legitimate sites
operational_patterns: Use of recognized web frameworks and CMS with standard HTML structure
Consistent navigation menus and footer links matching the domain
Use of official brand logos and images hosted on official domains
Standard user input fields with proper labels and accessibility features
No suspicious or hidden scripts that manipulate browser behavior
normal_thresholds: form action URLs must belong to the same domain or trusted subdomains
hidden input fields should not contain suspicious or encoded data
number of external scripts from untrusted domains should be zero or minimal
no overriding of native browser APIs via JavaScript
URL length and domain complexity within typical ranges for the brand

current_threats: phishing attacks targeting major brands (e.g., Telekom, Instagram, Microsoft, Telegram)
use of sophisticated obfuscation and API hooking to evade detection
credential harvesting via fake login forms
malicious redirects and tracking via hidden pixels
domain impersonation and use of free hosting platforms for phishing
emerging_patterns: increasing use of multi-modal data (HTML + URL) for detection
advanced JavaScript manipulation to bypass browser security
use of legitimate external resources to increase trust
complex URL structures with brand names embedded in subdomains
social engineering content localized in multiple languages
risk_factors: high similarity of phishing pages to legitimate sites
use of dynamic JavaScript to alter page behavior
hidden form fields and tracking pixels
non-standard or suspicious form submission endpoints
lack of HTTPS or mismatched SSL certificates
threat_landscape.threat_sophistication: high - attackers employ advanced web techniques and social engineering to bypass traditional detection

detection_rules: flag pages with form action URLs not matching the main domain or known trusted domains
detect JavaScript code that overrides or hooks native browser APIs (e.g., navigator.geolocation)
identify presence of hidden 1x1 pixel images used for tracking or data exfiltration
monitor for mismatch between page title/meta description and domain name
detect URLs with excessive subdomain levels or brand name obfuscation
monitoring_recommendations: continuous monitoring of URL structures for suspicious patterns
analysis of embedded JavaScript for API hooking or obfuscation
inspection of form elements and their submission endpoints
tracking of external resource domains and their trustworthiness
use of multi-modal analysis combining HTML content and URL features
threshold_suggestions: alert if form action URL domain differs from page domain by more than 1 level
flag if more than 2 hidden 1x1 pixel images are present
detect if JavaScript overrides native APIs with custom functions
consider URLs with more than 3 brand name tokens in subdomain as suspicious
trigger alerts for login forms with non-HTTPS or invalid SSL
pattern_matching: use regex to detect suspicious form action URLs (e.g., containing 'free.php', 'process.php')
pattern match JavaScript code that redefines navigator.geolocation methods
match URLs with brand names embedded in unusual subdomain patterns
identify hidden input fields with encoded or suspicious values
detect presence of tracking pixels with 1x1 size and hidden attributes
